title: A resident keeps its old code after a src/ edit
body:
Restart the resident before verifying: run node src/cli.js ui (it retires the stale one) or pipe a session-start payload into node hooks/run.cjs session-start, then check that GET /api/resident reports stale:false. index.html is read on every GET / and needs only a browser refresh. The resident is not part of the session's MCP server: stopping it keeps the mcp__dd__* tools; reconnect the MCP server with /mcp when its own answers say its code is stale. A restart changes the audit UI key, so give the user the new address.

Why: The resident fingerprints src/ and refuses hooks once it changes (409 build_stale), but keeps serving UI routes with its old code until the next prompt or session start replaces it, and the prompt that triggers the replacement gets no recall. A new route then returns 404, or a new field reads as undefined in the page, while the source is correct.

evidence.summary: One resident per machine, found through ~/.dd-data/resident.json; ensureResident replaces a stale one.
staleCode() guards hook calls only (409 build_stale); UI routes keep answering with the loaded code; uiKey is random per start.
The MCP server calls ensureResident and does not host the UI in-process.

v1.trigger: After editing src/ in a DD checkout while a resident is running, or when a route or field just added to src/ui/server.js is missing from the running audit UI (404, or 'Cannot read properties of undefined' in the browser console)
